privacy-policy.title: Privacy Policy
intro: Your privacy matters to us. This Privacy Policy explains how Naadu Nalam collects, uses, stores and protects information when you use our website and services. It applies to this website and to orders fulfilled through it.

items: Order information — your name, delivery address, pin code, email address and phone number, collected at checkout so we can process, pack, deliver and invoice your order.
Account information — if you create an account, your username, email address and saved delivery addresses.
Enquiry information — the name, email address and message you submit through our contact form.
Technical information — your IP address, browser type and pages viewed, recorded in standard server logs and used to keep the site secure and working correctly.
To process, pack and deliver your order, and to contact you about it.
To handle refunds, replacements and delivery issues under our Refund Policy.
To respond to enquiries you send us.
To manage your account, where you have created one.
To keep records required for tax and accounting purposes.
To detect and prevent fraud and misuse of the website.

blocks.text: We send marketing email only if you have asked us to. Every marketing email includes an unsubscribe link, and unsubscribing does not affect order-related messages.
We do not collect or store your card, UPI or net-banking details.
Where an online payment method is offered, payment is completed on the payment provider’s own secure systems and we receive only a confirmation of the result.
Where you choose Cash on Delivery, payment is collected at the time your order is handed to you.
We use cookies that are necessary for the site to function, including keeping items in your cart and keeping you signed in.
Most browsers let you block or delete cookies through their settings. Please note that blocking necessary cookies may stop parts of the website, such as the cart and checkout, from working correctly.
We share your information only where it is needed to run the service:

items: Delivery partners — your name, address and phone number, so your order can be delivered.
Sellers on our marketplace — where an item is supplied by an independent seller, the details needed to prepare and dispatch that item.
Payment providers — where you pay online, to process and verify the transaction.
Our hosting and IT providers — who store and process data on our behalf under contract.
Authorities — where we are required to disclose information by law.

blocks.text: We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it for third-party advertising.
This website is served over an encrypted HTTPS connection. Access to order and customer data is limited to people who need it to fulfil orders and support customers.
No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, but we take reasonable steps to protect your information against loss, misuse and unauthorised access.

items: Order and invoice records are retained for as long as required under applicable tax and accounting rules.
Account details are kept until you ask us to delete your account.
Contact-form enquiries are kept only as long as needed to deal with the enquiry.

blocks.text: Under India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, you may ask us to:

items: Confirm what personal data we hold about you and obtain a copy of it.
Correct data that is inaccurate, incomplete or out of date.
Erase your personal data, where we are not required to retain it.
Withdraw a consent you previously gave, at any time.
Nominate another person to exercise these rights on your behalf.

blocks.text: To make a request, write to us using the contact details below. We will respond within a reasonable period.
This website is not directed at children, and we do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 18. Orders should be placed by an adult.

If you have a concern about how your personal data has been handled, contact our grievance officer at hello@naadunalam.in or +91 90921 14630, marking your message for the attention of the Grievance Officer.
If you are not satisfied with our response, you may escalate the matter to the Data Protection Board of India.
We may update this policy as our services change or as the law requires. The current version is always the one published on this page.
We typically reply within one business day.

Address Chennai, Tamil Nadu 600001, India
Hours Monday to Saturday, 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM. Sunday closed.

refund-policy.title: Return & Refund Policy
intro: We want you to have a positive experience with Naadu Nalam. This policy explains when returns, replacements or refunds may be available for eligible orders. Because we sell food and farm products, and many items are perishable, please review this policy before placing an order.

blocks.text: The following may be eligible for a refund or replacement:

items: Damaged, spoiled or incorrect items — reported within 24 hours of delivery.
Non-perishable products — unopened and in their original packaging, reported within 7 days.

blocks.text: This policy applies to marketplace orders in the same way as to items we supply directly, including items supplied by independent sellers on our marketplace.
If an item arrives damaged or spoiled, report it within 24 hours of delivery. Please send us:

items: Your order number
The product name and details
Photographs or a short video of the issue, where applicable
A brief description of what is wrong

blocks.text: Photographs help us resolve the issue quickly and, where needed, raise it with the seller or delivery partner.
If you receive a product different from what you ordered, report it within 24 hours of delivery with your order number, the item you received and a photograph where possible.
Where stock allows, we may offer a replacement of the correct item instead of a refund. If a replacement is not available, an approved refund will be processed as set out below.

If you have a genuine concern about the quality or condition of an item you received, tell us within 24 hours of delivery with your order number, photographs where applicable and a description of the problem. We will review each case individually.
Farm produce is a natural product, so size, colour and appearance will vary from the photographs shown on the website. Natural variation of this kind is not in itself a quality defect.
The following are not eligible for return:

items: Fruits, vegetables and frozen items, once delivered in acceptable condition.
Products that have been consumed, or stored improperly after delivery.

blocks.text: This does not affect your rights where an item was damaged, spoiled or incorrect on delivery and reported within 24 hours.
Requests are reviewed individually against the eligibility rules above. Once a refund is approved:

items: Orders paid online — the refund is returned to the original payment method within 5–7 business days.
Cash on Delivery orders — there is no original payment method to refund to, so we will ask you for a UPI ID or bank account and process the refund there within the same 5–7 business days.

blocks.text: The time taken for the amount to appear in your account after we process it may depend on your bank or payment provider.
Where stock allows, we may offer a replacement instead of a refund for damaged or incorrect items. We will confirm this with you before arranging it.
If you need to cancel an order, contact us as soon as possible with your order number.
Orders are packed within 24–48 hours on business days, and perishable items are bought against the day’s orders, so cancellation may not be possible once an order has been packed or dispatched.

We may also refuse or cancel an order ourselves for fraud prevention, stock availability or delivery restrictions, as set out in our Terms of Service. Where we do, anything you have already paid for that order is refunded.
Email us with your order number, photos of the issue and a brief description. We typically reply within one business day.

many-sellers-one-basket.title: Many Sellers, One Basket: How Buying Direct Works Here
intro: Naadu Nalam is built as a marketplace rather than a single shop. Independent growers and small producers each keep their own store page, and your basket can draw from several of them at once.

blocks.text: Most produce reaches a city through layers that erase where it came from. We take the opposite approach: every listing belongs to a seller with a page you can open. If a batch of drumstick or a jar of forest honey is good, you can go back to the same person for the next one.

A typical order might combine cluster beans from one grower, cold-pressed sesame oil from a small mill, and cardamom from a spice seller. You pay once. Behind the scenes each seller is notified for their own part of the order, which is why items occasionally arrive in more than one packet.

Smaller producers cannot promise the same crate every week of the year, and we would rather show an honest gap than pad the catalogue. When something is out of season it leaves the shelf until it is genuinely ready again.
If you are new here, the simplest place to start is a small mixed order: a vegetable or two, one pantry staple, and one thing you have not cooked with before.

cold-pressed-vs-refined-oils.title: Cold-Pressed vs Refined: Why Our Oils Taste Like the Seed
intro: Open a bottle of cold-pressed sesame oil next to a refined one and the difference is immediate. One smells like toasted seed; the other smells like almost nothing. That gap is the whole argument for pressing cold.

blocks.text: The seed is crushed slowly, without added heat. Because temperatures stay low, the aromatic compounds and natural colour survive the process. Refining runs hotter and uses further steps to neutralise and deodorise the oil, which produces a clear, long-lasting, largely flavourless product.

Cold-pressed oils have a lower smoke point, so they are happier at moderate heat than in a hard deep-fry. Our sesame oil suits tempering, rice mixes and pickles, where its flavour is the point. Groundnut oil is the more neutral of the two and handles everyday sautéing comfortably.

Keep the bottle capped, away from the stove, and out of direct light. Cold-pressed oil has not been stripped of the compounds that make it taste good, which also means it does not sit indefinitely. Buy the size you will actually finish in a couple of months.
A sediment layer at the bottom is normal and not a fault. Tip the bottle gently before pouring.

choosing-your-honey.title: Forest Multi-Floral or Tulsi Infused: Picking Your Honey
intro: We stock two honeys, and they are not interchangeable. One is a broad forest harvest; the other is built around tulsi. Knowing which is which saves you from using the interesting one where it will be wasted.

blocks.text: Bees foraging across mixed forest flowering produce a darker, deeper honey whose character shifts a little with each harvest. That variation is the nature of a multi-floral crop, not a defect. It is the one to reach for when honey is doing the heavy lifting: drizzled over curd, stirred into warm water, or spread plainly on bread.

Lighter in body with a distinct herbal note running through it. It works best where you want that note to register — in tea, in a morning tonic, or taken on its own by the spoon. Bury it in a heavily spiced dish and you will not taste what you paid for.

Raw honey sets over time, particularly in cooler months. Granules at the bottom of the jar are a sign it has not been heat-treated into permanent clarity. Stand the jar in warm water for a few minutes and it loosens again. Avoid boiling it.
Both keep well in a sealed jar at room temperature. Use a dry spoon — water introduced into the jar is the main thing that shortens honey’s life.

red-rice-or-sona-masoori.title: Red Rice or Sona Masoori: Matching the Grain to the Meal
intro: Our two most-ordered grains sit at opposite ends of the same shelf. Sona masoori is the light, familiar daily rice. Red rice is heavier, nuttier and keeps its bran. They suit different meals.

blocks.text: A short, soft grain that cooks quickly and stays fluffy. It is the right choice when the rice is a backdrop — under sambar, rasam or a coconut-heavy curry — because it absorbs without turning claggy. Rinse until the water runs mostly clear, then cook with roughly two parts water to one part rice.

Because the bran layer stays on, red rice takes longer, drinks more water, and arrives with a firm bite and a faintly earthy flavour. Soak it for thirty minutes if you can, use closer to two and a half parts water, and give it time. It stands up to strong, sour and spiced dishes that would flatten a softer grain.

Plenty of households keep both and alternate — red rice on days when the meal is simple and the rice should be interesting, sona masoori when the curry is the star. If you are moving toward whole grains, blending the two in the same pot is an easier transition than switching outright, though you will need to soak the red rice first so they finish together.

ragi-flour-millet-kitchens.title: Ragi Flour: The Millet Tamil Kitchens Never Gave Up
intro: Ragi never really left South Indian kitchens. While polished grains took over city shelves, finger millet held its place in porridge, in kali, and in the flat breads people grew up on.

blocks.text: The easiest introduction is a thin porridge. Whisk a couple of spoons of ragi flour into cold water first — always cold, or it will seize into lumps — then cook it out over a low flame, stirring, until it thickens and loses its raw smell. Finish it savoury with buttermilk, salt and shallot, or sweet with a little jaggery.

Ragi has no gluten, so a dough made from it alone will not stretch. Pat it out by hand rather than rolling, or cut it with wheat flour if you want something more forgiving. A one-to-two ratio of ragi to wheat gives you the colour and flavour without fighting the dough.

It is a whole grain with a good deal of fibre, and it is filling in a way that lasts — which is the practical reason it survives as a breakfast and as a first food for children. Nothing exotic; just a grain that does its job.
Store the flour in an airtight jar. Whole-grain flours carry their natural oils and go stale faster than refined ones, so buy in quantities you will get through.

cooking-country-vegetables.title: Drumstick, Snake Gourd and Cluster Beans, Cooked Simply
intro: The vegetables that move fastest through our stalls are also the ones people are least sure how to cook. All three below are better treated plainly than dressed up.

blocks.text: Cut the pods into finger-length pieces and leave the tough skin on — you scrape the soft interior out at the table. Drumstick’s flavour is released by simmering, which is why it belongs in sambar and in thin, tamarind-sour gravies rather than in a dry fry. Add it early enough to soften but not so early that it collapses.

Split it lengthways, scrape out the spongy core and the seeds, then slice into half-moons. It holds a great deal of water, so it wants a hot pan and no lid — covered, it stews in its own liquid and turns grey. A quick poriyal with mustard seed, urad dal and grated coconut is all it needs.

The most assertive of the three, with a bitterness that is the point rather than a flaw. Top, tail and chop, then either blanch briefly before frying or cook them long and slow with tamarind. Undercooked cluster beans are unpleasantly squeaky; give them longer than instinct suggests.
None of these keep especially well once cut. Buy what you will cook within two or three days and store them dry, not in a sealed bag.
